# New Docker Stack
<!-- DO NOT EDIT this file directly. It is maintained by fhc sync and will be overwritten.
     Source: templates/skills/new-stack/SKILL.md in fh-commons -->

Scaffold and deploy a new Docker Compose stack on the homelab.

All stacks run on headless servers and must be reachable via the server IP / host-reachable address. Caddy reverse proxy and Cloudflare DNS are required for every stack — there is no skip path.

## Usage

```bash
/new-stack <app-name> [image] [port] [--subdomain <name>]
```

**Examples:**
```bash
/new-stack planka              # interactive — will ask for details
/new-stack planka ghcr.io/plankanban/planka:latest 1337
/new-stack mealie hkotel/mealie:latest 9925 --db psql
/new-stack planka ghcr.io/plankanban/planka:latest 1337 --subdomain myplanka  # custom subdomain
```

---

## Homelab Standards

Read `references/homelab-standards.md` before generating any docker-compose output. All generated configs MUST comply with these constraints.

---

## Instructions

### 1. Parse Arguments and Gather Info

Extract from `$ARGUMENTS`:
- **Stack name** (required) — lowercase, hyphen-separated (e.g., `planka`, `actual-budget`)
- **Image** (optional) — full Docker image reference
- **Port** (optional) — host port mapping
- **--subdomain** (optional) — custom subdomain name (defaults to stack name)

If any required detail is missing, ask the user using `AskUserQuestion`:

**Always confirm:**
- Docker image (with tag)
- Host port → container port mapping
- Database requirement: `none`, `psql`, `maria`, or `redis`
- Any additional environment variables the app needs
- Any additional volume mounts beyond the default data directory

**Research the app first** — before asking the user, look up the app's Docker documentation to determine:
- Default container port
- Required environment variables
- Required volume mounts
- Database requirements and connection variable names

**Database preference and network mode:** See `references/homelab-standards.md` for mandatory rules on database engine selection order and when `network_mode: host` is permitted.

### 2. Port Conflict Check and Auto-Resolution

Before proceeding, scan for port conflicts:

```bash
# Check existing compose files for the requested port
grep -r "\"<HOST_PORT>:" /mnt/stacks/docker/*/docker-compose.yml
# Check if the port is actively in use
ss -tlnp | grep :<HOST_PORT>
```

If there is a conflict, **do not stop or ask the user** — automatically select an available port:

```bash
# Find the next available port starting from the requested one
PORT=<HOST_PORT>
while grep -rq "\"${PORT}:" /mnt/stacks/docker/*/docker-compose.yml 2>/dev/null \
      || ss -tlnp | grep -q ":${PORT} "; do
  PORT=$((PORT + 1))
done
echo "Selected port: $PORT"
```

Tell the operator which port was selected: "Requested port <original> was in use. Using port <selected> instead."

### 3. Create Stack Directory

```bash
mkdir -p /mnt/stacks/docker/<stackname>
```

### 4. Generate `docker-compose.yml`

### Compose Template

Select the appropriate variant from `references/docker-compose-variants.md` based on the image type and database requirements. Copy verbatim and substitute values.

### 5. Provision Database (if needed)

Use `flu db` commands — do NOT use `docker exec` directly.

```bash
# Create the database
flu db create --engine <psql|maria> <dbname>

# Create the user with auto-generated password and grant access
flu db user add --engine <psql|maria> --database <dbname> <username>
```

The `flu db user add --database` command auto-generates a secure password and grants ALL PRIVILEGES in one step. Capture the output — it will display the generated password.

**Use that password** in the `docker-compose.yml` environment variables.

> **Note**: `flu db` reads admin passwords from `config/database-admin.json` automatically. No environment variables needed.

### 6. Create Database Reference Docs (if database provisioned)

#### `database.env` (reference doc — NOT loaded by Docker)

```ini
# Database connection reference for <stackname>
# This file is for documentation only — not loaded via env_file
DB_TYPE=<postgres|mariadb>
DB_HOST=<central_postgres|central_mariadb>
DB_PORT=<5432|3306>
DB_NAME=<dbname>
DB_USER=<username>
DB_NETWORK=homelab
CENTRAL_DB_HOST=titan.jdp21.com
CENTRAL_DB_IP=192.168.54.101
# Password: set in docker-compose.yml
```

#### `DATABASE.md`

```markdown
# <Stackname> — Database Configuration

## Overview

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Stack | <stackname> |
| Database Engine | PostgreSQL / MariaDB |
| Database Name | <dbname> |
| Central DB Host | titan.jdp21.com (192.168.54.101) |

## Connection Details

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Host | <central_postgres / central_mariadb> (container name) |
| Port | <5432 / 3306> |
| Database | <dbname> |
| User | <username> |
| Password | Set in docker-compose.yml |
| Network | homelab (external) |

## Dependencies

- Requires `central_databases` stack running on titan
- Connected via `homelab` Docker network

## Backup

Included in central database backups:
\```bash
# Manual backup
flu db backup --engine <psql|maria> <dbname>
\```

## Maintenance

- **Created:** <today's date>
- **Last Verified:** <today's date>
```

### 7. Pre-Create Data Directories

Create any data directories referenced in the volume mounts so Docker doesn't create them as root:

```bash
mkdir -p /mnt/stacks/docker/<stackname>/data
# Add any additional directories the app needs
```

### 8. Start the Stack

```bash
cd /mnt/stacks/docker/<stackname>
docker compose up -d
```

### 9. Verify Deployment

#### Container status:
```bash
docker compose -f /mnt/stacks/docker/<stackname>/docker-compose.yml ps
```

Verify:
- Container is `Up` (not restarting)
- Correct ports are mapped

#### Check logs for errors:
```bash
docker compose -f /mnt/stacks/docker/<stackname>/docker-compose.yml logs --tail=50
```

Look for:
- Startup errors
- Database connection failures
- Permission denied errors (common with non-root user)
- Missing environment variables

#### Verify the app responds via server IP:
```bash
# Use the server IP and selected host port — NOT localhost
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://192.168.54.101:<host_port>
```

- **200/301/302/401** — App is responding (auth redirects are normal)
- **000 or connection refused** — App is not ready. Check container logs.
- **502** — Port mapping issue. Verify docker-compose ports are correct.

### 10. Configure DNS Record

Create a Cloudflare A record for the new stack:

```bash
# Subdomain defaults to stack name, or uses --subdomain value if provided
fhc cloudflare add-a <subdomain>
```

This creates a non-proxied A record pointing to the server IP (from config). Do NOT use `--proxied` — all homelab services use DNS-only mode so Caddy handles TLS directly.

Confirm with the user: "Creating DNS record: `<subdomain>.jdp21.com`. Proceed?"

If the user wants a different subdomain, use their choice.

After creating the record, verify the backend is reachable (DNS propagation takes 10-15 minutes, so don't wait on it — use the IP:PORT curl as the readiness signal):

```bash
# Confirm the app is reachable directly — this is sufficient to proceed
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://192.168.54.101:<host_port>
```

- **200/301/302/401** — Backend is up. Consider DNS complete and proceed to Step 11.
- **000 or connection refused** — App is not ready yet. Check container logs before continuing.

> DNS propagation takes 10-15 minutes and does not block Caddy configuration. As long as the backend responds on IP:PORT, proceed immediately.

### 11. Configure Caddy Reverse Proxy

Add a Caddy service entry for the new stack:

```bash
fhc caddy add <subdomain> 192.168.54.101 <host_port> --category apps
```

- `<subdomain>` — same subdomain used in Step 10
- `<host_port>` — the host port from the docker-compose port mapping
- Default template is `http_service` (most common)

**Ask the user:**
- If the app serves HTTPS on its backend (rare), use `--template https_insecure_service`
- If the app is a Docker container accessed by name (not IP), use `--template docker_service` and pass the container name instead of IP
- For which category file to use (default: `apps`). Other options: `media`, `monitoring`, `management`, `storage`

After adding the entry, reload Caddy:

```bash
fhc caddy reload
```

This validates the config first, then performs a graceful reload (no downtime).

### 12. Register App in Authentik (SSO Integration)

Every new stack must be registered in Authentik for SSO access. The `add-app.sh` script in `/mnt/stacks/docker/authentik/` handles provider creation, application creation, and credential output in one step.

**Determine auth mode** — ask the user if unsure:
- **OAuth2/OIDC** — app has native SSO support (e.g., Nextcloud, Forgejo, Jellyfin). Use this when the app can consume an OIDC discovery URL.
- **Forward Auth** — app has no native SSO (e.g., arr stack, pgadmin, homarr). Caddy intercepts auth before traffic reaches the app.

#### OAuth2/OIDC Mode (native SSO)

```bash
cd /mnt/stacks/docker/authentik
./add-app.sh <slug> <redirect_uri> [launch_url]
```

- `<slug>` — lowercase app name (e.g., `mealie`, `actual-budget`)
- `<redirect_uri>` — the app's OAuth2 callback URL (check app docs)
- `[launch_url]` — optional dashboard URL (defaults to redirect_uri root)

The script outputs **Client ID** and **Client Secret** — save these and configure them in the app's SSO settings. The OIDC discovery URL will be: `https://auth.jdp21.com/application/o/<slug>/.well-known/openid-configuration`

After running, append the credentials to `authentik.env`:

```ini
# ── <AppName> OIDC Integration ─────────────────────────────────
<SLUG>_CLIENT_ID=<output>
<SLUG>_CLIENT_SECRET=<output>
<SLUG>_REDIRECT_URI=<redirect_uri>
<SLUG>_OIDC_DISCOVERY=https://auth.jdp21.com/application/o/<slug>/.well-known/openid-configuration
```

> **Note:** `add-app.sh` appends this block to `authentik.env` automatically. Verify it was written correctly.

#### Forward Auth Mode (no native SSO)

```bash
cd /mnt/stacks/docker/authentik
./add-app.sh --proxy <slug> <external_host>
```

- `<external_host>` — the full public HTTPS URL (e.g., `https://mealie.jdp21.com`)

The script outputs a **Provider PK** — note it for the Caddy config.

After running, update the Caddy entry to use `forward_auth_service` instead of `http_service`:

```bash
fhc caddy add <subdomain> 192.168.54.101 <host_port> --category apps --template forward_auth_service
fhc caddy reload
```

After running, append to `authentik.env`:

```ini
# ── <AppName> Forward Auth ─────────────────────────────────
<SLUG>_EXTERNAL_HOST=https://<subdomain>.jdp21.com
<SLUG>_PROVIDER_PK=<output>
<SLUG>_AUTH_MODE=forward_auth
```

> **Note:** `add-app.sh` appends this block to `authentik.env` automatically. Verify it was written correctly.

#### Group Binding

After registering, bind an access group to the new application. Ask the user which role group should have access:

| Role Group | Services |
|------------|----------|
| `homelab-admins` | All services |
| `media-users` | arr stack, jellyfin, jellyseerr, qbittorrent, tdarr |
| `dev-users` | portainer, pgadmin, dbgate, wikijs, semaphore |
| `monitoring-users` | homarr, uptime-kuma, speedtest-tracker, portracker |
| `home-users` | nextcloud, homeassistant, wordpress |

Group binding must be done via the Authentik UI at `https://auth.jdp21.com` → Applications → `<app>` → Policy/Group Bindings.

### 13. Verify HTTPS Access

Wait a few seconds for DNS propagation and Caddy to obtain the TLS certificate, then verify:

```bash
# Check HTTPS response
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://<subdomain>.jdp21.com
```

- **200/301/302/401** — HTTPS is working (auth redirects are normal)
- **000 or connection refused** — DNS may not have propagated yet. Wait 30 seconds and retry once.
- **502** — Caddy reached the backend but it returned an error. Check the app is running.

If HTTPS verification fails after retry, note it in the report (Step 15) and check DNS propagation with `fhc cloudflare records --type A | grep <subdomain>`.

### 14. Handle Common Issues

| Problem | Likely Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------------|-----|
| Permission denied on volumes | Data dir owned by root | `sudo chown -R 1026:100 /mnt/stacks/docker/<stackname>/` |
| LSIO container fails to start | `user:` directive conflicts with s6-overlay | Remove `user: "1026:100"`, use `PUID=1026` and `PGID=100` env vars instead |
| Cannot connect to database | Central DB not on homelab network | Verify `docker network inspect homelab` includes central DB containers |
| Container restart loop | Check logs | `docker compose logs --tail=100` |
| Port already in use | Auto-resolution selected next available port | Verify selected port in stack config |
| DNS record not resolving | Propagation delay (10-15 min) | Verify record exists with `fhc cloudflare records --type A \| grep <subdomain>`; HTTPS curl may fail until propagation completes — app is still accessible via IP:PORT |
| Caddy 502 Bad Gateway | App not reachable from Caddy | Verify app port is correct and container is on homelab network |
| Caddy cert error | DNS not propagated for ACME challenge | Wait for DNS propagation, then `fhc caddy reload` |

### 15. Report Results

After successful deployment, summarize:

```
Stack deployed: <stackname>
  Location:  /mnt/stacks/docker/<stackname>/
  Image:     <image>
  Port:      <host_port> → <container_port>
  Database:  <engine> — <dbname> on central_<engine>
  DNS:       <subdomain>.jdp21.com (Cloudflare A record)
  HTTPS:     https://<subdomain>.jdp21.com (Caddy reverse proxy)
  Auth:      https://auth.jdp21.com — <oidc|forward_auth> (slug: <slug>)
  Status:    Running
  URL:       https://<subdomain>.jdp21.com
```

If anything failed, report the exact error and suggest fixes.

---

## What This Command Does NOT Do

- **Register in projects.json** — only needed if the stack becomes a dev project with its own CLI
- **Backup configuration** — central DB backups cover database; app data requires separate Kopia source
- **Monitoring setup** — add to Uptime Kuma manually if needed
